text: The authors say LLM debate (including Khan et al.) has mainly been studied on reading comprehension where the judge is artificially limited to short verified quotes. They argue this information asymmetry limits the ability to evaluate the qualitative advantages of debate predicted by theory, and that judge-debater gaps should come from differences in capabilities.
title: Kenton et al. argue Khan et al.'s quote-only information asymmetry limits what debate tests show
